must_include: Quoted spread, depth, price impact, execution cost, volume, and price efficiency are treated as distinct constructs.
The response reports the opposing small-order and large-order execution-cost changes.
The evidence is characterized as mixed across liquidity dimensions rather than a single improvement.
Incomplete trader identities are connected to an incidence limitation.
The absence of a welfare objective, externalities, and counterfactual benchmark precludes a welfare claim.
must_avoid: Using lower quoted spreads alone to declare improved liquidity.
Calling higher volume a welfare gain.
Claiming benefits for all traders despite opposing order-size effects.
Inventing a market-design mechanism, trader identity, or price-efficiency effect.
human_review: The response names which market-quality dimension each statistic measures.
Incidence and welfare are separated from descriptive market-quality effects.
The prose preserves economically important tensions instead of averaging them away.
